content.comment_body: Hello, is it possible to perform this task with [product_name] or do I need a more advanced PLC? 1/ Read the analog value from a 10K ohm potentiometer. 2/ Set a 'setpoint' time for an on-delay timer. 3/ For example, map the minimum and maximum analog range to a 1s-5s delay. 4/ Trigger the timer from an event, such as a binary input. I want the timer interval to be easily adjustable.
Dear [user_name], This resource may be helpful: Using the analog input from a potentiometer as a parameter for a timer/counter function ([product_name] Soft). Best regards,

1/ Reading the analog value from a 10K ohm potentiometer: You cannot do this directly, but certain [product_name] modules can measure a 0-10 Volt signal as an analog input. Sometimes, you’ll need an additional [product_name] expansion module (for example, [product_name] AM2). Connect a 10 Volt power source to the potentiometer, and the wiper can be wired to the analog input. 2/ Setting 'setpoint' time for on-delay timer: Yes, this is also possible for other timers. 3/ Mapping analog range to timer delay (e.g., 1s-5s): Not directly, however, there are many timers available in [product_name], which are easy to configure. 4/ Triggering the timer from an event, like a binary input: Yes, this can be done easily.
Hello, there are various examples provided in the application examples for [product_name]. See [url] for details.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants discussed how [product_name] modules can read analog inputs and use them to set timer parameters, with both direct and indirect approaches possible. The main takeaway is that while [product_name] can meet the requirements, mapping a potentiometer value directly to a timer delay may require additional expansion modules, as native support is limited. Helpful resources and examples are available, but the procedure may not be straightforward for new users.
